passage:
Chat, 7:40 pm

Eshaan: Result is out. I didn't clear it.
Eshaan: Please don't say anything.
Mridul: Come, let us eat.
Eshaan: Not hungry bhai. Go with the others, I'm just dragging everyone down 😔
Mridul: I'm at your hostel gate. Paratha stall, ten minutes. No talk about marks.
Eshaan: You'll get bored of me.
Mridul: Not possible. Bring your ID card, the guard is strict 🙂
Eshaan: [later] ate two parathas. Thank you.
Eshaan: Still feel terrible though.
Mridul: Fine. Terrible and full. Retake plan tomorrow or next week, your call.
Eshaan: Tomorrow. Maybe. 🙏

qa.q: What did Mridul say to Eshaan right after hearing the result?
Why did Eshaan first tell Mridul to go with the others?
qa.a: Eshaan felt undeserving and believed that being around would drag everyone down, so tried to push Mridul away.

qa.q: What could Eshaan do next about the exam?
qa.a: Let the kindness settle first, as the two parathas did, and then start on a retake plan tomorrow or next week, at Eshaan's own pace. 🙂

qa.q: How does Mridul seem to read Eshaan's "you'll get bored of me"?
qa.a: Mridul answers lightly with "Not possible" and keeps to the plan, which suggests Mridul hears sadness, not a real wish to be left alone.

grounding: Shows a friend's simple compassion ('come, let us eat') after a failed result, without a lecture, letting the person feel held.

passage:
Friday night

The results came at noon. I didn't clear the prelims, second year in a row. I'm Bhupen. I sat in the cyber café staring at my roll number not being there, and I wanted to disappear.

Santosh called. I nearly didn't pick up. I didn't want his pity, didn't feel I deserved anyone being nice to me. He didn't ask about marks. He said, "Come, let's eat. The dhaba near the bridge. I'm leaving now."

We ate rotis and dal fry and he talked about his cousin's wedding, the cows that walked into the tent. I laughed. Actually laughed. He never once said "next year" or "you should have".

Walking back, I told him I didn't know what to do next. He said, "Not tonight. Tonight you ate." I felt held.

Tomorrow I'll look at the paper again, and think about what comes next. Tonight, I ate.

qa.q: Where did Santosh take Bhupen to eat?
qa.a: To the dhaba near the bridge.

qa.q: What was Bhupen feeling when Santosh called?
qa.a: Bhupen felt ashamed and undeserving, wanting to disappear, and nearly didn't pick up.

qa.q: Why was letting Santosh's kindness in a good first step?
qa.a: Eating and laughing without a lecture settled Bhupen, so planning the next step could wait until the next day.

qa.q: How might Santosh see his role that night?
qa.a: Santosh seems to see his job as simply being there and feeding his friend, not fixing the result or giving advice.

grounding: The diary shows a young person who fails an exam and is simply fed by a friend without a lecture, letting kindness settle them before planning.

passage:
Siddharth: didn't get it. final round rejection
Manoj: ah no. I'm sorry yaar
Siddharth: third company this month. I'm clearly not good enough
Manoj: where are you right now
Siddharth: bus stop outside their office
Manoj: come to mine. amma made biryani
Manoj: we'll just eat. no talking about interviews
Siddharth: I don't want to be a sad guest
Siddharth: you've done enough for me already
Manoj: you're not a guest, you're family. come let's eat
Siddharth: ...ok. 30 mins

Later
Siddharth: thanks. I needed that more than I knew
Siddharth: tomorrow can you help me look at the feedback email
Manoj: yes. tonight sleep

qa.q: Where was Siddharth when Manoj asked?
qa.a: Siddharth was at the bus stop outside the company's office.

qa.q: What was Siddharth feeling after the rejection?
qa.a: Siddharth felt discouraged and not good enough, and also undeserving of more kindness from Manoj.

qa.q: How did Siddharth let Manoj's kindness help?
qa.a: Siddharth accepted the invitation to just eat, let it settle the panic, and only then planned to look at the feedback the next day.

qa.q: How does Manoj see Siddharth after the rejection?
qa.a: Manoj sees Siddharth as family who needs company and food, not advice or a lecture.

grounding: The chat shows a young person who fails a job interview being invited to eat by a friend without a lecture, letting the kindness settle things before planning.
